key_lines: He highlighted the rising demand for goods and services among India’s 1.4 billion people and said that growing imports also indicate opportunities for domestic industry and international investors.
items.text:
Posted On:
 12 OCT 2026 2:22PM by PIB Delhi
 

 
 
 

 
 
 Union Minister of Commerce and Industry, Shri Piyush Goyal, emphasised a twin-track approach of engaging with the world’s best technologies and identifying areas with significant job and business potential. 


 Addressing the ‘Dilli Dialogue: Policies for a Future-Ready India’ in New Delhi, today, he highlighted the importance of creating opportunities for businesses, startups and young people. The Minister said, “We want to be a part of the global marketplace. Providing opportunities for people, providing opportunities for jobs, for our startups, for our youth to come up with newer ideas.” 


 Shri Goyal highlighted India’s expanding engagement with global markets through Free Trade Agreements (FTAs), emphasising the opportunities these agreements create for Indian businesses and youth. He said that India’s partnerships with developed economies could benefit both sides, with India offering strengths in textiles, footwear, agriculture and food processing while gaining access to advanced technologies and high-quality electronic equipment. 


 Emphasising India’s approach to global engagement and self-reliance, Shri Goyal said, “We are not closing the doors of India to the world. We are, in fact, opening them wider.” 


 Shri Piyush Goyal, also emphasised the importance of setting ambitious targets for India’s economic growth and exports while speaking at the event, Shri Goyal referred to the trillion-dollar export target and expressed confidence in India’s ability to achieve it and highlighted the importance of pursuing ambitious national goals as part of the country’s journey towards ‘Viksit Bharat 2047.’ 


 The Minister said that India’s ambition of becoming a developed nation by 2047 is supported by a roadmap identifying sectors that will contribute to the country’s growth. He highlighted the rising demand for goods and services among India’s 1.4 billion people and said that growing imports also indicate opportunities for domestic industry and international investors. He noted that increasing demand for electronics and white goods could encourage investment in domestic manufacturing, including semiconductor factories. 


 Shri Goyal identified tourism as a sector with substantial potential to generate employment and create new business opportunities. He said that artificial intelligence could improve the efficiency of tourism promotion, while human experiences would remain central to the sector. He stated, “AI can only add to the efficiency of promoting tourism. But otherwise, human experiences will always be AI proof.” 


 He also highlighted India’s culinary heritage and regional diversity, referring to the potential of Indian food traditions and products such as filter coffee, rasam, idli and dosa. 


 Shri Goyal also highlighted India’s demographic advantage, noting that its young population offers opportunities at a time when many economies are experiencing ageing populations. He referred to the demand for Indian workers in countries such as Germany and Japan and highlighted the potential for Indian professionals to contribute to international markets. Shri Goyal also highlighted the trust placed in Indian workers internationally, stating that Indians are respected for their honesty and their commitment to caring for others. 


 Shri Piyush Goyal expressed confidence that India would emerge as a global hub for car manufacturing, stating that international automobile manufacturers would increasingly manufacture in India as market demand reaches a viable scale. Referring to the quotas permitted for car imports from the United Kingdom and the European Union, Shri Goyal explained that these largely covered expensive cars, while the lower-priced segment had not been opened. Citing the examples of luxury automobile manufacturers establishing manufacturing plants in Pune after initially testing the Indian market, Shri Goyal highlighted India’s potential to attract global automobile manufacturers and strengthen its position in global car manufacturing. 


 Emphasising the importance of quality in strengthening India’s global competitiveness, the Minister called for collective efforts by policymakers, industry stakeholders and institutions, including the Bureau of Indian Standards and the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India, to improve quality standards. 


 Shri Goyal concluded by emphasising that if India adopts and practises world-class quality standards, no power on earth can stop it and the world is India’s to capture.

items.title: IMD Dedicates Cyclone Warning and Marine Weather Services Decision Support System to the Nation on 12th October, 2026
items.text:
Posted On:
 12 OCT 2026 10:21PM by PIB Delhi
 

 
 
 

 
 
 The India Meteorological Department (IMD) dedicates Cyclone Warning and Marine Weather Services Decision Support System (DSS), an interactive WebGIS-based platform, to the nation on 12th October 2026 . The launch took place during the bi-annual Pre-Cyclone Exercise Meeting for the post-monsoon season (October-December), 2026 under the chairmanship of Dr. Mrutyunjay Mohapatra, Director General of Meteorology, IMD and 3rd Vice President of World Meteorological Organisation. The above DSS platform for public is available on IMD website ( www.mausam.imd.gov.in ) and Regional Specialised Meteorological Centre (RSMC) website ( www.rsmcnewdelhi.imd.gov.in ). The url of the above web-based platform is given below: 


 https://dss.imd.gov.in/dwr_img/GIS/marine.php 


 


 DSS demonstrating observed & forecast track & intensity alongwith cone of uncertainty and district-wise rainfall warning 


 The DSS is a user-friendly, interactive platform that brings critical cyclone and marine weather information together in one place, making it easier for users, including disaster management authorities, government agencies and the general public, to understand potential hazards and their likely impacts. Through interactive maps and visualisations of cyclone tracks, intensity, winds, rainfall, storm surge and rainfall forecasts for river catchments, the platform helps users access relevant information and make informed decisions. It aims to bridge the gap between weather forecasts and their practical use, enabling better preparedness, timely action and enhanced public safety during cyclones and other severe weather events. 


 


 DSS demonstrating observed & forecast track & intensity alongwith wind distribution and district-wise rainfall warning 


 


 
 DSS demonstrating observed & forecast track & intensity alongwith wind distribution and storm surge warning 




 
 The occasion holds special significance as IMD successfully predicted Very Severe Cyclonic Storm Phailin (2013) and Very Severe Cyclonic Storm Hudhud (2014) (both incidentally crossed coast on 12th October, 2013 and 2014 respectively) and marked important milestones in India’s disaster preparedness, earning international recognition for the country’s early-warning capabilities. 


 IMD has been conducting this meeting bi-annually since 2008. The exercise serves as a vital platform for reviewing preparedness for the ensuing cyclone season, assessing progress on previous action points, sharing IMD’s latest initiatives and addressing operational challenges. It also fosters close liaison and coordination among IMD, disaster management authorities, defence forces, state governments and other user agencies, ensuring that forecasts and warnings are effectively utilised for timely action on the ground. 


 The meeting witnessed participation from more than 30 organisations across the country, with approximately 230 participants, including 180 joining online and 50 attending in person . The participating organisations included the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA), National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), Indian Navy (IN), Indian Air Force (IAF), Indian Coast Guard (ICG), Central Water Commission (CWC), Press Information Bureau (PIB), state disaster management authorities and fisheries departments. Scientific and technical organisations included the India Meteorological Department (IMD), National Centre for Medium Range Weather Forecasting (NCMRWF) and Indian Institute of Technology (IIT). Representatives from coastal states and Union Territories, including West Bengal, Odisha, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Kerala, Karnataka, Goa, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Lakshadweep, Daman & Diu, Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Puducherry also participated. Delegates from various ministries and departments, including the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, Ministry of Heavy Industries, Department of Consumer Affairs, Directorate General of Light House & Light Ships (DGLL), and other sectoral stakeholders, attended the meeting. The participation provided an important platform for strengthening inter-agency coordination, sharing operational requirements and enhancing preparedness for the upcoming cyclone season. 


 The meeting commenced with a presentation on the activities and recent advancements of the IMD in the field of cyclone warning and marine weather services, followed by a review of the Action Taken Report on the recommendations of the Pre-Cyclone Exercise Meeting held in April. A live demonstration of the newly launched, user-oriented Decision Support System (DSS) showcased its interactive features and capabilities to provide location-specific information on cyclones and associated hazards. The demonstration was followed by valuable comments, suggestions and feedback from participating stakeholders, aimed at further improving the platform and enhancing its operational utility. 


 The meeting reaffirmed IMD’s commitment to strengthening early-warning services , enhancing inter-agency coordination and translating accurate forecasts into timely action to minimise loss of life and property during cyclones. 




 


 A total of 230 Disaster Managers and stakeholders participated in the meeting

items.text:
Posted On:

 As Prime Minister Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana (PMDDKY) completed one year of implementation on 11 th October 2026, the Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India, organised an event today to mark the occasion at the Bharat Ratna C. Subramaniam Auditorium, National Agricultural Science Complex (NASC), PUSA, New Delhi. The event was attended by Union Ministers, Secretaries of Central Ministries/Departments, Central Nodal Officers under PMDDKY, senior officers of the Central Government, and more than 370 delegates from the states including District Collectors, district-level functionaries, agricultural scientists and progressive farmers of DDKY districts. 


 


 Addressing the gathering Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare and Rural Development, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan stated that the first year had focused on establishing strong foundations, while the coming year must be dedicated to delivering visible and measurable outcomes on the ground. He highlighted the importance of improving agricultural productivity, increasing cropping intensity, strengthening irrigation and water management, facilitating access to agricultural credit, promoting high-value agriculture, improving post-harvest infrastructure and enhancing farmers’ incomes. 


 


 Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan emphasised that the ultimate measure of PMDDKY’s success would be the meaningful difference it makes to the lives of farmers. He called upon all stakeholders to strengthen coordination, accelerate implementation and focus on measurable improvements in agricultural outcomes and sustainable farm incomes. The participation of Allied Ministries/Departments reflected the importance of a coordinated, whole-of-government approach to agricultural development. 


 


 Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan reaffirmed the Government of India’s commitment to working with State Governments, district administrations, scientific institutions and farmers to translate district action plans into tangible results. The coming year will focus on scaling up successful interventions and improving outcomes across all identified districts, with the overarching vision of making all 100 PMDDKY districts truly “Dhan-Dhaanya” — rich in grain and rich in prosperity. 


 


 Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan also emphasised that the Khet Bachao Abhiyan, scheduled to be organised across all States from 22 October to 30 November 2026, aims to promote soil health through the balanced and judicious use of fertilisers. The Minister encouraged all State Governments and concerned authorities to actively participate in the campaign and ensure its successful implementation. He highlighted the importance of adopting sustainable agricultural practices to maintain soil fertility, protect the environment, and preserve natural resources for future generations. 


 


 In his welcome address, the Secretary, Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, highlighted the district-centric approach of the scheme, under which action plans are prepared by districts in accordance with their soil conditions, rainfall, cropping patterns, water availability, infrastructure and the needs of their farming communities. He acknowledged the contribution of State Governments, District Collectors, District Nodal Officers, Central Nodal Officers, Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) scientists and field functionaries in implementing the scheme. He also underscored the importance of the District Dhan-Dhaanya Samitis in coordinating planning and implementation. The scheme monitors district performance against 121 indicators through a dedicated dashboard, with monthly rankings encouraging transparency and healthy competition among districts. 


 


 As part of the programme, representatives of three PMDDKY districts shared their experiences and innovative initiatives. Gadchiroli district presented its work on water conservation and drought resilience , Alluri Sitharama Raju district highlighted initiatives for the promotion of high-value horticulture , and Banka district showcased the Lilawaran Natural Farming Land Revival Model . The presentations demonstrated how locally tailored interventions, supported by convergence and farmers’ participation, can address agricultural challenges and generate replicable solutions.

 Union Minister for Communications and Development of North Eastern Region (DoNER), Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, today inaugurated development projects and laid foundation stones of new initiatives worth ₹331 crore, in Mizoram.Shri Scindia is on two-day visit of Mizoram. 


 Upon his arrival in Aizwal, the Union Minister proceeded to Tuivamit and inaugurated five project worth ₹102 Crore. Union Minister also laid foundation stone of five projects of ₹228.54 crore. Projects cover critical sectors including road connectivity, power transmission, water supply, healthcare, education, sports and cultural infrastructure. 


 Addressing the gathering in the presence of Mizoram Chief Minister Pu Lalduhoma and other dignitaries, Union Minister Scindia said that the development initiatives reflected the Government of India's commitment to transforming connectivity into economic opportunities and improving the quality of life across Mizoram. 


 Describing Mizoram as a land of majestic mountains and even greater aspirations, the Union Minister said, "Geography may shape the landscape. It must never shape the limits of the people." 


 He emphasised that the occasion was not merely about inaugurating infrastructure or laying foundation stones, but about creating opportunities for farmers, entrepreneurs, young people and communities across the state. 


 


 Northeast Emerging as an Engine of India's Growth--- 


 Highlighting the growing economic significance of the North Eastern Region, Jyotiraditya M. Scindia said that while India is recording economic growth of around 7–7.5%, the Northeast is increasingly emerging as a major contributor to the country's growth trajectory. 


 He observed that it would not be an exaggeration to describe the North Eastern Region as an engine driving India's development forward. 


 The Union Minister noted that this was his 35th visit to the North Eastern Region and said that every visit strengthened his commitment to the development of the eight Ashtalakshmi states. 


 "Every time I come here, I go back recharged and with a renewed commitment towards the Ashtalakshmi states," he said. 


 Referring to his longstanding association with Chief Minister Pu Lalduhoma, Shri Scindia fondly recalled the close relationship between the Chief Minister and his late father. In a lighter moment, he remarked that he represented the second generation of that relationship and appreciated the Chief Minister's youthful energy and enthusiasm. 


 Shri Scindia also highlighted the region's extraordinary natural beauty and ecological wealth, stressing that development must proceed alongside environmental conservation. 


 


 Connectivity Transforming Mizoram's Development Landscape --- 


 The Union Minister highlighted the significant improvements in Mizoram's connectivity through roads, railways and air transport, observing that the state was becoming increasingly connected not only through infrastructure but also through stronger bonds between people. 


 He described the 51.38-kilometre Bairabi–Sairang railway line as a historic milestone that brought Mizoram onto India's railway map and transformed access to major economic centers. 


 The railway connectivity has facilitated the movement of more than 15 lakh passengers through over 1,100 train trips, linking Aizawl with Guwahati, Kolkata and Delhi. The introduction of the Sairang–Silchar service has further strengthened connectivity with the Barak Valley. 


 Highlighting another landmark achievement, Shri Scindia referred to the arrival of the first Food Corporation of India food-grain rake at Sairang in March 2026, carrying approximately 26,000 quintals of rice from Punjab in 42 wagons. 


 He said that the direct movement of food grains from Punjab to Mizoram by rail would have been difficult to imagine a decade ago and demonstrated how improved connectivity was bringing distant regions of the country closer together. 


 Referring to tourism, Shri Scindia noted that Mizoram had recorded 4,94,362 domestic tourist visits and 7,389 foreign tourist visits during the first six months of 2026, reflecting the state's growing appeal as a tourism destination. 


 


 Mizoram Ginger Mission to Strengthen Farmers' Livelihoods -- 


 Highlighting the state's agricultural potential, Shri Scindia described Mizo ginger as a unique strength and economic identity of Mizoram. 


 He said that the ₹189.79 crore Mizoram Ginger Mission would bring nearly 20,000 farming households into an integrated value chain encompassing cultivation, processing, branding, connectivity and access to national and international markets. 


 The Union Minister emphasised that the objective was not merely to increase ginger production but to ensure that farmers and local communities received a greater share of the economic value generated. 


 "Mizo ginger is Mizoram's USP; our mission is to make sure the value stays where the ginger grows," he said. 


 ₹331 Crore Development Push Across Key Sectors -

 The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare will observe World Mental Health Day on 10 October 2026 , reaffirming the Government of India's commitment to making mental healthcare accessible, affordable, inclusive and people-centred. This year's global theme, “Lived experiences heard: real voices, real change,” underscores the importance of listening to individuals with lived experiences of mental health conditions and ensuring their voices contribute to shaping responsive mental health policies and services. 


 At the heart of India's efforts to improve access to mental healthcare is Tele MANAS (Tele Mental Health Assistance and Networking Across States) , which has emerged as an important pillar of the country's mental healthcare delivery system. Through its national toll-free helpline 14416 , Tele-MANAS is providing free, confidential and round-the-clock mental health counselling and support, enabling people to seek professional assistance easily, irrespective of their geographical location or socioeconomic background. 


 Tele-MANAS: Making Mental Health Support Just a Phone Call Away 


 Launched on 10 October 2022, Tele-MANAS has rendered yeoman service in bridging gaps in access to mental healthcare by bringing timely counselling, emotional support and professional guidance directly to people through a simple telephone call. 


 Since its launch, Tele MANAS has received 47,75,644 calls, with 53 operational cells across all 36 States and Union Territories , as of October 2026. This extensive reach reflects the growing importance of accessible, technology-enabled mental health services in addressing diverse mental health needs across the country. 


 Through 14416 , individuals experiencing emotional distress, anxiety, stress, sleep-related concerns or other mental health challenges can connect with trained counsellors without having to travel to a healthcare facility for initial support. Available 24 hours a day, seven days a week, and supported by multilingual services, the helpline makes it easier for people to seek help at a time and place convenient to them. 


 The service is particularly significant for people residing in rural, remote and underserved areas, where access to specialised mental healthcare facilities may be limited. By offering a confidential and supportive platform, Tele-MANAS is also helping address hesitation associated with seeking mental health assistance and encouraging individuals to reach out early. 


 Beyond initial counselling, the programme facilitates access to specialised mental health professionals and appropriate referral services wherever required, helping ensure continuity of care through linkages with the wider public healthcare system. 


 Growing Public Engagement Reflects the Importance of Accessible Mental Healthcare 


 The increasing utilisation of Tele-MANAS highlights the importance of having a readily accessible platform where individuals can seek support without fear of stigma or discrimination. 


 An analysis of 13,35,275 recorded caller profiles indicates that women account for 43.78% (5,84,587) of callers , while men constitute 54.18% (7,23,427). The substantial participation of women highlights the role of telephone-based counselling in providing a convenient and supportive avenue for seeking mental healthcare. 


 The service has also witnessed significant engagement among young and working-age populations, with individuals aged 18–45 years accounting for 73.2% of recorded caller profiles . 


 The range of concerns reported by callers, including emotional distress, stress related to examinations, workplaces and relationships, anxiety and sleep disturbances, demonstrates the importance of accessible mental health support in everyday life. 


 By providing a platform where individuals can speak openly, receive guidance and be connected to appropriate services, Tele-MANAS is contributing to a broader shift towards recognising mental health as an integral part of overall health and well-being. 


 MANN Jaagriti: Taking Mental Health Awareness to Communities 


 As part of World Mental Health Day 2026, the Ministry is also taking forward MANN Jaagriti , a structured community awareness and engagement initiative aimed at strengthening mental health literacy, reducing stigma and encouraging timely help-seeking. 


 The initiative seeks to move beyond one-time awareness activities by promoting sustained community engagement through schools, colleges, workplaces, health facilities and other community platforms. 


 Through locally relevant activities, States and Union Territories will encourage open conversations around mental health, promote early identification of mental health concerns and create greater awareness about available services, including Tele-MANAS. 


 The initiative will also encourage the involvement of healthcare professionals, educators, community workers, youth, families, caregivers, civil society organisations and persons with lived experience of mental health conditions. 


 By bringing mental health conversations into everyday community settings, MANN Jaagriti aims to foster supportive environments where seeking mental health assistance is recognised as a positive and important step towards well-being.

items.title: 9 Days SHILP SAMAGAM MELA 2026 Underway In Mysuru Since October 11
items.text:
Posted On:
 12 OCT 2026 7:40PM by PIB Delhi
 

 
 
 

 
 
 The SHILP SAMAGAM MELA 2026 is underway at the Mysuru Dasara Exhibition Grounds at Mysuru in Karnataka, being organized by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, since October 11. 


 The 9 Days Mela upto October 19, aims to provide a marketing platform for products made by beneficiaries from Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes and Safai Karamcharis, including artisans supported by the three National Corporations functioning under the Ministry, namely the National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), the National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC) and the National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC). 


 A senior official in the Ministry said the initiative seeks to strengthen market linkages for artisans, promote traditional craftsmanship and create sustainable livelihood opportunities for the target groups. 


 He said the Ministry has been organising SHILP SAMAGAM MELAS since 2022, and 975 artisans have been benefited through 13 such fairs organised so far. 


 The Mysuru edition is the first SHILP SAMAGAM MELA of the financial year 2026–27. 


 The official said a total of 83 stalls have been put up at the Mela, out of which 80 have been allotted to artisans, including 37 women artisans. Food stalls serving traditional delicacies have also been set up for visitors. 


 The Mela features artisans from 12 States and Union Territories, including Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Karnataka, Kerala, Rajasthan, Puducherry, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Telangana, Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh, he added. 


 The Official informed that the exhibition showcases a wide range of traditional products, including handicraft items, handloom sarees, spices, pickles, incense sticks, honey products, block-printed products, Kanjivaram sarees, leather goods, wooden toys, bags and purses, terracotta products, artificial jewellery, rosewood wall hangings, and bed and cushion covers. The platform enables artisans to display their products to a wider audience and connect with prospective customers, while promoting India's diverse cultural heritage and traditional skills. 


 


 The official further said that SHILP SAMAGAM MELA also serves as a platform to disseminate information about the schemes and programmes of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment and its three national corporations—NSFDC, NBCFDC and NSKFDC. The initiative seeks to enhance awareness about available assistance and development opportunities for eligible beneficiaries, while encouraging entrepreneurship and economic empowerment. 


 The Ministry has also introduced BHARAT TULIP (Traditional Artisans’ Upliftment Livelihood Programme) to expand market access for products made by the target groups through various digital platforms in India and abroad. Under this initiative, products are branded as BHARAT TULIP to enhance their visibility and facilitate online sales. The programme aims to strengthen artisans' livelihoods while preserving traditional art forms and promoting India's rich craftsmanship to a wider audience. 


 The Official said the Ministry facilitates the participation of artisans by providing free stalls and support covering travel expenses, daily allowance, transportation of goods, and meals, including lunch and dinner. This assistance helps artisans participate in the mela and showcase their products without bearing stall rental costs and specified participation-related expenses. 


 It is pertinent to mention that during the Financial Year 2026–27, the Ministry proposes to organise additional SHILP SAMAGAM FAIRS At Guwahati, Dilli Haat In New Delhi, Jodhpur And Lucknow. 


 The Ministry and its three National Corporations will also participate in major exhibitions, including the India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, from November 14 to 27, 2026, and the Surajkund Mela in Faridabad in February 2027. 


 Through initiatives such as SHILP SAMAGAM MELA and BHARAT TULIP, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment continues to promote market access, entrepreneurship and livelihood opportunities for artisans from the target groups, while supporting the preservation and wider recognition of India's traditional arts and crafts.
